Shaving the incision site immediately before spinal surgery may increase the rate of postoperative infection. This is because shaving can remove the protective lining over the wound, making it more susceptible to bacterial entry and subsequent infection.

It's essential to note that while shaving the incision site may increase the risk of infection, this effect is likely to be small in most cases, and other factors such as surgical technique, patient health, and antibiotic use will play a much larger role in determining the overall risk of postoperative infection.
